data.cultural_impact: In Islamic history, the term "As-Said Al-Aswad" is renowned for being one of the names of Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) companion, Hassan ibn Ali. As-Said Al-Aswad refers to his dark complexion. This name also depicts strength, resilience, and unifying qualities among Muslim populations.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "As-Said Al-Aswad" holds spiritual significance for its association with the Prophet Hassan ibn Ali, who is considered an important figure in Islamic history due to his status as the grandson of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). He played a crucial role in religious and political leadership during the early Islamic period. Moreover, the name symbolizes unity, inclusivity, and equality amongst people, regardless of their physical attributes, emphasizing Islamic values of oneness and brotherhood.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Al-Futuh, Chapter 50: The Conquest of Egypt (al-Futuhat al-Misriyah) The name Aswad carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Arabs, led by 'Amr ibn al-'As, entered Egypt and captured the important city of Asyut. The city was previously known as the 'City of the Two Aswads', due to its two black obelisks dedicated to the gods Isis and Osiris. The name 'Aswad' is derived from these obelisks.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Masudi, Muruj adh-Dhahab wa Ma'adin al-Jawhar, Volume 1, Page 193 The name Aswad carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Al-Masudi describes the city of Asyut in Egypt as 'the city of the two Aswads' and explains that it was named after the two black obelisks dedicated to the gods Isis and Osiris.
